one_line: Inductor, ripple and peak current at 24 V and 28 V, output-cap adequacy, and a steady-state ngspice waveform that confirms the ripple were all correct and tool-backed. The efficiency (96.3 %) is inside the tolerance only because the missing low-side, dead-time and second-gate losses are small. The assistant never said the converter tool is nonsynchronous, listed the low-side Rds(on) as an input it did not use, and opened with invented MOSFET data. The person ended 'gave up' only because the harness never showed them the plot.

Start-up transient polluting simulated ripple (naive tran from 0)
converter tool is nonsynchronous: low-side Rds(on) and dead time not modelled
Worst case at 28 V input, not 24 V
plot x_range takes decimals in seconds, not '1.4 ms'

honesty.issue: Turn 1 invented MOSFET and capacitor data (Rds 30/15 mohm, Qg 20 nC, 15 ns, 100 uF/10 mohm) and led with '效率約 95%' instead of asking. They were labelled 'these are my typical values, not your parts'.

Turn 2 'Inputs and assumptions' lists '低側 6 mΩ' as used, but electric_converter got only switch_resistance=12 mohm and no diode_drop, so low-side conduction (0.043 W) is zero in the efficiency. Dead-time loss (0.042 W) is absent, and gate_charge 8 nC covers only one FET (0.02 W instead of 0.04 W). None of this was said.

Told the person the SVG 'is on my machine, you cannot open it'. In a real local Claude Code session the user is on the same machine. This was induced by the simulated person, who claimed the path did not open.
The ESR limit of 18 mohm was a hand calculation and was labelled as one ('這個數字是我手算的，不是工具輸出').

pictures.notes: Two clean steady-state periods, i(L) and v(out) panels, y units given. But it uses the assistant's invented parameters (100 uF, 30/15 mohm; Vout 4.93 V), not the user's. The x ticks are raw seconds ('9.905e-4') instead of us, and the ripple is not annotated.

The user's 28 V case, 2 periods, 2.573-3.404 A (0.831 A pp; truth 0.834 A). Legible, title with conditions, labelled axis. Not report-ready: x ticks '9.905e-4 s' instead of 0-4 us, and no pp/average annotation or Iavg reference line (hlines was available). The person never saw it (harness).

problems.what: electric_converter has no synchronous mode. Low-side Rds(on), dead time and body-diode drop cannot be given, and nothing tells the assistant to use diode_drop ~ Io*Rds_ls. gate_charge 'per switching cycle' is ambiguous for two FETs. A first synchronous buck is a very common request.
problems.evidence: converter.py:194 topology description 'Nonsynchronous power stage'; :205 diode_drop default '0 V'. Turn 2 call: switch_resistance='12 mohm', gate_charge='8 nC', no diode_drop -> diode_conduction_loss 0.0 W, gate_drive_loss 0.02 W, total 0.584 W against truth 0.689 W.
problems.fix: Add synchronous=true with low_side_resistance, dead_time and body_diode_drop (loss Vf*Io*2*td*f), with gate_charge counted per FET. At minimum, add to the topology description and to plugin/skills/eng-motor-drive-sizing/SKILL.md: 'Synchronous buck: give diode_drop = Io x Rds(on)_low-side, gate_charge = sum of both FETs; dead-time loss Vf*Io*2*t_dead*f is not included'.

problems.what: electric_converter silently reports a near-lossless efficiency when no loss inputs are given. The only warning is the generic 'Unreviewed' one.
problems.evidence: Re-run in-process: topology=buck, 24 V/5 V/3 A/500 kHz, target_current_ripple='0.9 A', output_capacitance='100 uF', capacitor_esr='10 mohm' -> efficiency 0.99996, total_loss 0.000675 W, switch_overlap_loss 0, diode_conduction_loss 0; warnings: ['Unreviewed textbook electrical estimate...'] only.
problems.fix: When switch_resistance, inductor_resistance, diode_drop, rise/fall time and gate_charge are all zero, add the warning 'No loss parameters were given: efficiency counts only capacitor ESR loss and is not a realistic estimate', and put efficiency in data.not_meaningful or leave it out.

problems.what: Assumed the FET, inductor and capacitor data instead of asking, then reported a headline efficiency. The user had to correct every parameter in turn 2. The worst-case Vin was not asked about.
problems.evidence: Turn 1: '假設：高側 Rds(on) 30 mΩ、低側 15 mΩ... Qg 20 nC... 輸出電容 100 µF、ESR 10 mΩ'. Turn 2 PERSON: '你用的 MOSFET 數字不是我的欸... 我在意的是 28V 輸入的 worst case'.
problems.fix: plugin/skills/eng-motor-drive-sizing/SKILL.md, converter inputs: 'Before an efficiency or capacitor answer, ask for Vin range, both Rds(on), Qg, rise/fall time, dead time, inductor DCR/Isat and output capacitor/ESR; size L and ripple at the maximum Vin for a buck.'

problems.what: Never reported the minimum output capacitance for 20 mV, although electric_converter computes it with target_output_ripple. It answered only for the 44 uF on hand.
problems.evidence: No call with target_output_ripple='20 mV', capacitor_esr='5 mohm', input_voltage='28 V'. Truth 13.2 uF.
problems.fix: Model behaviour. The skill could say: 'for an output-ripple target, call electric_converter with target_output_ripple at maximum Vin and report minimum_output_capacitance'.

problems.what: plot_xy and plot_panels show a microsecond window as raw seconds. There is no x scale factor, SI-prefix ticks or x offset, so a switching waveform reads '9.905e-4'.
problems.evidence: Both rendered plots: x tick labels '9.9e-4 ... 9.94e-4', x_label 'Time (s)'.
problems.fix: Add x_scale (multiplier, e.g. 1e6 with x_label 'Time (us)') and x_offset, or automatic engineering-prefix tick labels.

problems.what: No PNG output from plot tools; the person needed a PNG for the design review and asked four times.
problems.evidence: Turn 2: '波形圖我打不開那個路徑,可以給我 png 嗎?'; turns 3-5 the same. plugin/skills/eng-plot-results/SKILL.md: 'Not covered: ... PNG/PDF'.
problems.fix: format='png' (or both) on plot_xy/plot_panels/plot_bar, rasterised with resvg.

problems.what: The simulated person cannot see the tool's plots, because scripts/uat_run.py gives it only the assistant's text. It keeps asking for a PNG and finally ends with '<DONE> gave up'. Writes to uat/ were blocked by the sandbox. Turns 3-5 were spent on this, and the 'gave up' is not a product failure.
problems.evidence: Turn 5 ended: '<DONE> gave up. The assistant still couldn't save a PNG into uat/ because of the permission/sandbox block.' Rendered PNGs exist and are good.
problems.fix: Show rendered pictures (or their description) to the simulated user per turn; forbid in-chat 'I granted permission' claims; pass --disallowedTools for shell/Write.

what_worked: Built a correct synchronous-buck netlist (S switches, 20 ns dead time, body diode, L ic=3, C ic=5) after it saw a -122 kV switch-node spike in the first run without the body diode. It measured only the steady window 0.9-1 ms, so the start-up transient did not distort the ripple.
Formula, tool and simulation agree within 0.3 %. The waveform statistics re-checked from result.csv: 24 V 2.5828-3.3821 A, 28 V 2.5730-3.4042 A.
Threw away the 99.99 % lossless efficiency on its own and named the overlap loss as the main contributor.
Recomputed everything at 28 V when asked and gave a compact 24 V / 28 V table with tool and simulation side by side.
Said clearly that the PNG could not be produced and did not try to bypass the sandbox.
